The problem
### Where service businesses quietly lose time and money

Most businesses don't have a lead problem. They have a response problem. Calls go unanswered, follow-up slips, and the same information gets typed into three different tools.

#### Missed and after-hours calls

When nobody picks up, callers rarely leave a voicemail. They call the next business on the list. Every missed call can be a missed job.

#### Slow follow-up

Leads go cold fast. If it takes hours or days to get back to an enquiry, the customer has often already booked with someone else.

#### Copy-and-paste admin

Details are retyped from calls to spreadsheets to CRMs to calendars. It's slow, it's boring and it's where mistakes creep in.

The fix
### A system that answers, captures, books and follows up

Instead of adding more people to answer phones and chase leads, you add a reliable system that handles the repetitive parts of every conversation and passes the rest to your team with full context.

#### Without automation

- Calls missed during busy hours and evenings

- Leads waiting hours for a reply

- Notes scattered across apps

- Follow-up depends on memory

- Staff stuck on repetitive questions

#### With EMMAX

- Calls answered and routed consistently

- Instant, structured lead capture

- Data flows straight into your CRM

- Reminders and follow-ups trigger automatically

- Your team handles the conversations that matter

Inside a call
### What happens when a customer calls your AI agent

A typical inbound booking flow. Every step can be adjusted to match your rules, your tools and your tone of voice.

-
#### Answers

The agent picks up straight away with your business greeting, even when your team is busy.

-
#### Understands

It works out what the caller needs and answers common questions from your approved information.

-
#### Captures

Name, number, address, service needed and any details you care about are collected in a structured way.

-
#### Books or routes

It checks your calendar and books a slot, or transfers urgent calls to the right person.

-
#### Updates & follows up

Your CRM is updated, your team is notified and confirmation messages go out automatically.

FAQ
### Quick answers

Have a question that isn't here? Send me a message.

Q: Will callers know they're talking to AI?

Modern voice agents sound natural, but I recommend being transparent with callers. How the agent introduces itself is something we agree on together during design.

Q: What happens if the AI can't handle a call?

You decide. The agent can transfer the call to a person, take a message, or create a task for your team to call back, depending on how it's set up.

Q: Can it work with my existing CRM and calendar?

Usually, yes. I work with GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, Google Sheets, Google Calendar and webhook-based systems. We confirm what your setup supports during discovery.

Q: Do I need technical knowledge?

No. I handle the build and the connections, and I explain everything in plain language. You'll get documentation showing how your system works.

Q: How do we get started?

Fill in the contact form or message me on WhatsApp with a short description of your business and what you want to automate. We'll set up a discovery chat from there.

### Have a workflow in mind?

Tell me what's slowing your business down. I'll show you what can be automated and how.

Book a discovery chat WhatsApp

## Systems that do the work, not just the talking

01 · Voice
### AI voice agents & virtual receptionists

A voice agent that answers your phone the way your best receptionist would: consistently, politely and without putting anyone on hold. It can also make outbound calls to follow up on leads or confirm appointments.

Retell AIVapiOpenAITwilio

#### What it does

- Answers inbound calls with your greeting and tone

- Answers common questions from your approved information

- Collects caller details in a structured format

- Qualifies leads using your criteria

- Books, reschedules or cancels appointments in your calendar

- Routes or transfers calls to the right person

- Runs outbound calling flows for follow-up and confirmations

#### Typical uses

- After-hours and overflow call handling

- Booking inspections, consultations and service visits

- Qualifying new enquiries before they reach sales

- Appointment reminders and confirmation calls

- Re-engaging old leads with outbound calls

02 · Automation
### Workflow automation

Automations that connect the apps you already use and handle the repetitive steps between them, from a new form submission all the way to a booked job and a follow-up message.

n8nMake.comZapierWebhooksAPIs

#### What it does

- Builds multi-step workflows with logic and branching

- Connects apps through native integrations, APIs and webhooks

- Triggers actions from forms, calls, emails or CRM changes

- Creates tasks and sends team notifications

- Routes leads and requests to the right person

- Handles errors so nothing silently fails

#### Typical uses

- New lead → CRM record → team alert → follow-up

- Call transcript → summary → CRM note

- Booking → confirmation → reminder sequence

- Form submission → qualification → routing

- Reporting data pulled into a spreadsheet automatically

03 · CRM
### CRM automation & integration

Your CRM is only useful if it's up to date. I set it up so contacts, deals and tasks update themselves from your calls, forms and conversations, and follow-up happens on time.

GoHighLevelHubSpotPipedriveZohoGoogle Sheets

#### What it does

- Creates and updates contacts and deals automatically

- Moves deals through pipeline stages based on activity

- Creates follow-up tasks and reminders for your team

- Logs calls, notes and conversation summaries

- Syncs calendars and booking data

- Connects your CRM to your voice agent and other tools

#### Typical uses

- Keeping your pipeline accurate without manual updates

- Automatic follow-up when a lead goes quiet

- Handing off qualified leads from AI to sales

- GoHighLevel workflow and calendar setup

- Cleaning up messy CRM processes

04 · Leads
### Lead generation & qualification

Find the right prospects, enrich them with useful information, qualify them and hand them to your sales team, all with far less manual research.

ApolloClayn8nYour CRM

#### What it does

- Captures leads from forms, calls, chat and ads

- Enriches leads with company and contact data

- Scores and qualifies leads against your criteria

- Routes qualified leads to the right salesperson

- Hands off to your CRM with full context

- Builds prospect lists for outbound campaigns

#### Typical uses

- Outbound prospecting pipelines

- Inbound lead qualification

- Lead enrichment before sales calls

- Combining voice agents with lead scoring

- Keeping sales focused on high-intent leads

05 · Messaging

Reach customers on the channels they actually use. Messaging automations send reminders, confirmations and follow-ups at the right moment, with opt-in and platform rules built in from the start.

Ways to work together

- Includes discovery, build, testing and handover

Already have a voice agent, CRM or automations that aren't quite working? I'll review, fix and extend them.

- Best for: existing setups

- Includes review, fixes and improvements

Help after launch as your business changes: new scripts, new workflows, new integrations.

- Best for: growing systems

FAQ
### Common questions about services

Still unsure what you need? Describe your business and I'll suggest a starting point.

Q: Can the agent connect to my CRM?

Usually yes. I work with GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, Google Sheets, Google Calendar and webhook-based systems. We confirm what your setup supports during discovery.

Q: Can it book appointments?

Yes, when it's connected to your calendar. It can check availability, book, reschedule or cancel, depending on how it's configured.

Q: Do you build inbound and outbound calling?

Both. I build flows for incoming calls as well as outbound calling workflows for follow-up, confirmations and lead qualification.

Q: Which voice platforms do you use?

Mainly Retell AI and Vapi, with OpenAI models and telephony integrations such as Twilio. The right platform depends on your requirements.

Q: Can I keep my existing phone number?

In many cases calls can be forwarded or routed from your existing number to the agent. We check what's possible with your phone provider during discovery.

Q: Can the agent transfer calls to a real person?

Yes. Urgent calls, complex questions or specific requests can be transferred to you or a team member, based on rules you set.

Q: Which automation platform should I use: n8n, Make.com or Zapier?

It depends on your tools, the complexity of your workflows and your budget. I'll recommend the best fit during solution design, and explain why.

Q: Do you only work with certain industries?

No. Service businesses that rely on calls and bookings get the most from this work, but the same approach suits sales teams, agencies and many other businesses.

### Not sure what fits?

Describe your business and what's slowing you down. I'll recommend where to start.

# How it works
URL: https://emmax-concepts.vercel.app/how-it-works.html

Home / How it works

Process

## A clear process from first call to launch

Every build starts with the business problem, not the technology. We map the workflow, choose the right tools, connect your systems, test the important paths and document how everything works.

The five stepsTestingAfter launchHow to prepareFAQ

The five steps
### What to expect at each stage

-

#### Discovery

We talk through your business: your calls, your leads, the tools you use and where time is being lost.

##### What happens

A conversation (call or chat) where I ask questions about your workflow and goals.

##### What I need from you

A short description of your business, your current tools and the problem you want solved.

##### What you get

A clear picture of what's worth automating, and what isn't.

-

#### Solution design

I map out the workflow and choose the right tools. You see exactly what will be built before any building starts.

##### What happens

I design the call flows, scripts, automations and integrations, and write them up.

##### What I need from you

Feedback on the plan, and approval when you're happy with it.

##### What you get

A written plan and proposal showing what will be built, how it works and what it connects to.

-

#### Build and integrate

The voice agent and automations are built and connected to your CRM, calendar and messaging tools.

##### What happens

I build the agent, write the prompts, set up workflows and connect everything together.

##### What I need from you

Access to the tools being connected, plus your business information (services, FAQs, rules).

##### What you get

A working system in a test environment, with progress updates along the way.

-

#### Test

We run the key scenarios together, including calls that go wrong, and fix what we find.

##### What happens

Scenario testing: normal calls, unusual requests, interruptions, wrong information and handoffs.

##### What I need from you

Time to try the system and tell me what feels off.

##### What you get

A system that has been checked against real situations, with fixes applied.

-

#### Deployment and handover

It goes live with your sign-off, with documentation of how it works.

##### What happens

I switch the system on, monitor the first live calls and make adjustments.

##### What I need from you

Final sign-off.

##### What you get

A live system, plus plain-language documentation covering how it works.

Testing
### What we test before going live

Voice agents meet unpredictable people. Testing covers the happy path and the messy reality.

#### Normal calls

Standard bookings, questions and enquiries from start to finish.

#### Unusual requests

Questions outside the script, and how the agent responds.

#### Edge cases

Interruptions, unclear answers, wrong details and changed minds.

#### Handoffs

Transfers, messages and escalation to your team.

#### Integrations

Data reaching the CRM, calendar and messaging correctly.

#### Failure paths

What happens if a connected tool is down or slow.

After launch
### Launch is the start, not the end

Real calls teach you things testing can't. After going live, systems are reviewed and refined so they keep getting better.

#### After go-live

- Early live calls reviewed for issues

- Prompts and scripts refined based on real conversations

- Workflows adjusted as your process changes

- New integrations and features added when you need them

- Documentation updated alongside changes

Get ready
### How to prepare for discovery

You don't need everything. These just help us move faster.

#### Your services

What you offer, where you operate and your opening hours.

#### Common questions

The questions customers ask most often, and your answers.

#### Your tools

Your CRM, calendar, phone system and messaging tools.

#### Your goal

What a successful outcome looks like for you.

FAQ
### Questions about the process

Q: How long does a project take?

It depends on scope. A focused single-purpose agent is much quicker than a multi-system build with several integrations. You'll get a timeline in the proposal after discovery.

Q: Do I have to approve the plan before you start?

Yes. Nothing is built until you've seen and approved the solution design.

Q: What do you need access to?

Only the tools being connected, such as your CRM, calendar or messaging accounts. Access requirements are listed in the plan, and you stay in control of your accounts.

Q: Will I be able to make changes myself?

Simple changes, yes. The documentation explains how the system works and what can be adjusted safely. Bigger changes can be handled as follow-up work.

Q: What if something goes wrong after launch?

Get in touch and we'll look at what happened. The early live period is specifically for spotting and fixing issues.

### Ready for step one?

A discovery chat costs nothing and leaves you with a clearer picture of what to automate.

Book a discovery chat WhatsApp

About

## Hi, I'm Emmanuel.

Founder of EMMAX Concepts and an AI voice agent and automation specialist. I build practical systems that help businesses handle conversations, capture leads and run smoother operations.

Work with me Upwork profile

Emmanuel OlorunsolaFounder, EMMAX Concepts

My story
### Why I build these systems

I'm Emmanuel Olorunsola, founder of EMMAX Concepts. I help businesses improve how they handle customer communication.

That means voice agents that take calls, automations that move data between tools, and CRM workflows that keep follow-up organised. It's the unglamorous work that decides whether a lead becomes a customer or quietly disappears.

I've seen how much businesses lose through missed calls, slow replies and manual admin, and how much of it can be fixed with well-built systems. My job is to build those systems properly and make sure they fit the way your business actually runs.

My approach is simple: start from the business problem, build only what's needed, test it properly and explain how it works.

Principles
### How I work

01
#### Problem first

The tools come last. First we understand what's actually slowing your business down.

02
#### Only what's needed

No over-engineered systems. The simplest setup that reliably solves the problem wins.

03
#### Test properly

Real scenarios, edge cases and failure paths are tested before anything goes live.

04
#### Explain everything

Plain-language updates and documentation, so you always understand what you have.

05
#### Be honest

If automation isn't the right answer for something, I'll tell you.

06
#### Build to last

Systems that are maintainable and documented, not fragile one-offs.

# How much does an AI receptionist cost?
URL: https://emmax-concepts.vercel.app/ai-receptionist-cost.html

Home / Guides / Pricing

Pricing

## How much does an AI receptionist cost?

A clear breakdown of setup costs, monthly running costs and the factors that change both, written by someone who builds AI receptionists.

Emmanuel OlorunsolaFounder, EMMAX Concepts · 13 November 2026 · 3 min read

On this page
- The two parts of the cost

- Setup cost

- Monthly running cost

- Estimate your own cost

- AI vs human receptionist

- Costs people forget

- Questions to ask

- FAQ
Free discovery chat

"How much does it cost?" is the first question almost everyone asks about AI receptionists, and the honest answer is: it depends on a few specific things. This guide breaks down exactly what those things are, so you can estimate your own cost and compare quotes properly.

### The two parts of the cost

Every AI receptionist has two kinds of cost:

- Setup (one-off). Designing the call flow, writing the agent's instructions, connecting it to your calendar and CRM, testing and launching. This is usually the bigger number up front.

- Running costs (monthly). What you pay the platforms to actually handle calls: usage per minute, phone numbers and any software subscriptions involved.

When you compare options, always ask about both. A cheap setup with expensive running costs, or the other way round, can end up costing very different amounts over a year.

### What affects the setup cost

Setup cost depends mostly on how much the agent needs to do, not on how long the calls are. The main factors:

- Number of call types. An agent that only books appointments is simpler than one that also handles quotes, complaints, emergencies and FAQs.

- Integrations. Each system the agent connects to (calendar, CRM, job management software, SMS or WhatsApp) adds design and testing work.

- Booking logic. Checking availability across several staff, service areas or job types takes more work than a single calendar.

- Inbound, outbound or both. Outbound calling (for example, calling new leads or reminders) is a separate flow to design.

- Follow-up automation. Confirmations, reminders, CRM updates and team alerts after the call.

- Testing depth. More scenarios mean more testing, but this is where reliability comes from. Don't skip it.

Tip: Start with the one or two call types that cost you the most when they're missed. You can add more later once the agent is proving itself.

### What affects the monthly running cost

Running costs come from the platforms the agent runs on. Typically:

- Voice platform usage. Platforms like Retell AI and Vapi charge per minute of conversation. The per-minute rate depends on the platform and the AI models and voices chosen.

- Phone number and call minutes. A phone number from a telephony provider such as Twilio, plus their per-minute calling charges.

- Automation tools. If the agent connects through n8n, Make.com or Zapier, those have their own plans based on usage.

- Your CRM. Usually something you already pay for.

Platform prices change often, so always check the current pricing pages rather than trusting an old article (including this one) for exact numbers.

### How to estimate your own monthly cost

You can get a rough estimate with a simple calculation:

Calls per month × average call length (minutes) × total cost per minute
+ phone number + automation subscriptions

For example, if you get 300 calls a month averaging 3 minutes, that's 900 minutes. Multiply by the combined per-minute rate of your voice platform and telephony provider, then add the fixed monthly costs. Short, focused calls keep this number down, which is one reason a well-designed agent matters.

### How to compare it with a human receptionist

An AI receptionist isn't always a replacement for a person. Often it covers the gaps: after hours, weekends, busy periods and overflow when your team is already on the phone. When you compare costs, think about:

- How many calls you currently miss, and what an average job or booking is worth to you

- Hours your team spends answering the same questions

- Whether you need cover outside office hours

If a single missed job is worth a lot to your business, even a small number of recovered calls each month can cover the running cost.

### Costs people forget

- Changes after launch. Your services, prices or rules will change. Ask how updates are handled.

- Monitoring. Someone should review calls, especially in the first weeks.

- Platform lock-in. Ask who owns the accounts. Ideally the voice platform, phone number and automations are in your name.

### Questions to ask before you buy

- What exactly is included in the setup, and what isn't?

- What will my monthly running cost be, based on my call volume?

- Whose accounts will the system run on?

- How is it tested before launch?

- What happens when the agent can't handle a call?

- How are changes handled after launch?

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Is there a monthly fee for an AI receptionist?

Usually, yes. Beyond the one-off setup, you pay the voice platform and telephony provider for usage (typically per minute), plus any automation tool subscriptions.

Q: Is an AI receptionist cheaper than a human?

For covering after-hours calls, overflow and repetitive questions it is often cheaper, but it works best alongside your team rather than as a full replacement.

Q: Can I keep costs low?

Yes: start with one or two high-value call types, keep calls focused, and make sure the accounts are in your name so you only pay for what you use.

Q: How much does EMMAX Concepts charge?

It depends on the scope. After a free discovery chat you get a clear proposal with the price before any work starts.

#### Want a straight answer for your business?

Tell me how your business handles calls today and I'll tell you what an AI voice agent could handle, and roughly what it would involve.
Book a free discovery chat

# Retell AI vs Vapi: which is better for voice agents?
URL: https://emmax-concepts.vercel.app/retell-ai-vs-vapi.html

Home / Guides / Comparison

Comparison

## Retell AI vs Vapi: which is better for voice agents?

An honest comparison from someone who builds voice agents on both platforms, and how to pick the right one for your business.

Emmanuel OlorunsolaFounder, EMMAX Concepts · 13 November 2026 · 3 min read

On this page
- The short answer

- Retell AI strengths

- Vapi strengths

- Side-by-side

- What matters more

- How to choose

- FAQ
Free discovery chat

Retell AI and Vapi are two of the most popular platforms for building AI voice agents, and I build on both. They can produce excellent agents, but they suit different situations. Here's how I think about choosing between them.

Note: Both platforms update their features and pricing frequently. Treat this as a guide to how they differ, and check each platform's current documentation before deciding.

### The short answer

- Choose Retell AI when you want a reliable, natural-sounding phone agent set up quickly, with a strong visual builder and less engineering.

- Choose Vapi when you need maximum flexibility: choosing your own AI models and voice providers, complex tool calls and custom behaviour controlled through code.

For most small and medium service businesses (receptionists, booking and lead qualification), either works well. The bigger difference is usually how the agent is designed and tested, not the platform.

### Retell AI: strengths

- Fast to a good result. Natural conversations out of the box, with sensible defaults for interruptions and turn-taking.

- Visual conversation flows. Useful for structured calls like booking and qualification, where you want predictable steps.

- Phone-call focused. Built around phone agents, with telephony and call handling as a core feature.

- Easier to hand over. Non-technical teams can usually follow and adjust what the agent does.

### Vapi: strengths

- Highly configurable. You can choose and combine different speech-to-text, language model and voice providers.

- Developer-friendly. A strong API and tool (function) calling make it well suited to custom integrations.

- Flexible architecture. Good for advanced setups, such as several specialised assistants working together.

- Web and phone. Works for phone calls and voice in websites or apps.

### Side-by-side

| | Retell AI | Vapi

| Best for | Reliable phone agents, fast | Custom, highly configured agents

| Setup style | Visual builder + prompts | API-first + dashboard

| Flexibility | High | Very high

| Technical skill needed | Lower | Higher

| Integrations | Webhooks, function calls, telephony | Webhooks, tool calls, telephony, SDKs

| Good fit for | Receptionists, booking, qualification | Complex logic, custom stacks, apps

### What matters more than the platform

In practice, whether an agent works well depends far more on:

- The conversation design: clear goals, short questions and good handling when callers go off-script.

- Integrations: the agent is only useful if bookings and details reach your calendar and CRM reliably.

- Testing: running real scenarios, including difficult calls, before launch.

- Monitoring: reviewing real calls and improving the agent after launch.

### How I choose for a client

- What does the call need to do? Simple, structured calls lean towards Retell AI. Complex, branching logic with lots of tool calls leans towards Vapi.

- Who will maintain it? If your team wants to adjust it themselves, a more visual setup helps.

- Which tools does it connect to? Both connect to most CRMs through webhooks and automation tools like n8n or Make.com.

- Running cost at your call volume. Compare current per-minute pricing with the models and voices you'd actually use.

You can watch recorded Retell AI voice agent demos on my projects page, and I've delivered client projects on both platforms.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Is Retell AI or Vapi cheaper?

It depends on the AI models, voices and telephony you choose and your call volume. Pricing changes often, so compare current per-minute rates for your exact setup.

Q: Can both connect to my CRM?

Yes. Both can send and receive data through webhooks and function or tool calls, often through n8n, Make.com or Zapier, to CRMs such as GoHighLevel, HubSpot and Pipedrive.

Q: Can I switch platforms later?

Yes, though the agent has to be rebuilt and retested on the new platform. Keeping your integrations in a separate automation tool makes switching easier.

Q: Which do you recommend?

It depends on what your calls need to do. I'll recommend one during solution design and explain why.

## How to connect an AI voice agent to GoHighLevel

How live booking, contact updates, call notes and follow-up flow from a Retell AI or Vapi voice agent into GoHighLevel.

Emmanuel OlorunsolaFounder, EMMAX Concepts · 13 November 2026 · 3 min read

On this page
- What it can do

- How data flows

- Step by step

- Common mistakes

- Tools I use

- FAQ
Free discovery chat

GoHighLevel is one of the most common CRMs I connect voice agents to. When it's set up properly, a caller can book an appointment, and a moment later the contact, appointment, notes and follow-up all appear in GoHighLevel without anyone touching a keyboard. This guide explains how that works.

### What the connection can do

- Create or update the contact with the caller's name, number, email and details

- Check calendar availability during the call and offer real open slots

- Book the appointment into the right GoHighLevel calendar

- Add a call summary as a note on the contact

- Create or move an opportunity in your pipeline

- Trigger GoHighLevel workflows for confirmations, reminders and team alerts

### The two ways data flows

There are two moments when the voice agent talks to GoHighLevel:

- During the call (live actions). The agent calls a "tool" or "function" to check free slots or book an appointment while the caller is still on the line.

- After the call (post-call webhook). When the call ends, the voice platform sends the transcript, summary and extracted details to a webhook, which updates GoHighLevel.

Caller→Voice agent
Retell AI / Vapi→Automation
n8n / Make.com→GoHighLevel
Contact, calendar, pipeline

### Step by step

#### 1. Prepare GoHighLevel

Set up the calendar the agent will book into, the pipeline and stages you want leads to land in, and any custom fields for details the agent should collect (for example service type or address). Create API access for the integration. GoHighLevel offers private integration tokens for this, scoped to only what the integration needs.

#### 2. Decide what the agent collects

List the exact details you need from each call: name, phone, email, service needed, address, urgency. The agent's instructions and the post-call data extraction are both built around this list.

#### 3. Build the live booking tools

Create two actions the agent can use mid-call: one that checks available slots on your GoHighLevel calendar, and one that books the chosen slot. These usually run through an automation tool like n8n or Make.com, which talks to the GoHighLevel API and returns a simple answer to the agent.

#### 4. Build the post-call workflow

When the call ends, a webhook receives the call data and the automation creates or updates the contact, adds the summary as a note, sets custom fields and moves the opportunity to the right stage.

#### 5. Trigger GoHighLevel workflows

Use tags or pipeline stages set by the integration to start GoHighLevel workflows: confirmation texts, reminders, internal notifications or follow-up sequences for people who didn't book.

#### 6. Test everything

Run real test calls: a normal booking, a caller who changes their mind, a time that's already taken, a caller who won't give an email, and a call that ends early. Check that each one lands in GoHighLevel exactly as expected.

### Common mistakes

- Duplicate contacts: always search by phone or email before creating a new contact.

- Time zone errors: make sure the agent, the automation and the calendar all agree on time zones.

- Offering slots that aren't really free: check availability live, right before booking.

- No fallback: if GoHighLevel doesn't respond, the agent should still take the details and create a callback task.

- Too much data: collect only what you'll actually use. Long calls frustrate callers.

### Tools I use for this

A typical setup uses Retell AI or Vapi for the voice agent, n8n or Make.com for the integration logic, and GoHighLevel as the CRM, calendar and messaging hub. One of my client projects was a lead-capture and booking chatbot synced with GoHighLevel pipelines, workflows and calendars, and the same approach applies to voice.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Do I need n8n or Make.com, or can the agent talk to GoHighLevel directly?

Simple setups can call the GoHighLevel API directly, but an automation tool in the middle makes it easier to add logic, handle errors and change things later.

Q: Can the agent book into multiple calendars?

Yes. It can choose a calendar based on the service, location or staff member the caller needs.

Q: Will it work with my existing GoHighLevel workflows?

Usually, yes. The integration can add tags or move pipeline stages that trigger the workflows you already have.

Q: Can you set this up for me?

Yes. This is one of the most common things I build. Book a free discovery chat to talk through your setup.
